title: Dashboard — User Manual
summary: How the customizable Dashboard works: widgets, layout, and the Export Briefing PDF.

sections.body:
Overview

The Dashboard is the landing page after login. It's a personal, drag-and-drop grid of KPI cards and charts — every user can build their own layout, and it's saved automatically per account.

Key Features

  • A catalog of widgets (Total Assets, Open Tickets, Low Stock, Devices Seen, Docs & SOPs, charts, Recent Activity, and more).
  • Drag-and-drop reordering and per-widget resizing (1, 2, or 4 columns).
  • "Export Briefing" — generates a PDF operations summary (key metrics, maintenance due, recent activity) for offline sharing.
  • Clicking the Node IP indicator in the top bar shows details about the device you're currently using.
  • A day/night theme toggle in the top bar.

Step-by-Step

  1. Click Add Widget (top-right of the dashboard) to browse the widget catalog and add one to your layout.
  2. Drag a widget by its handle to reorder it; use the resize control to change how many columns it spans.
  3. Click the × on a widget's toolbar to remove it — you can always add it back later.
  4. Click Export Briefing in the top bar whenever you need a shareable PDF snapshot of current operations.

Tips

  • Your layout is personal — changing it never affects what other users see on their own dashboards.
  • If a module you don't have permission for has no data, its widget still renders but shows zero/empty rather than erroring.
